## Refactor packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts

**File:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — **2,365 lines** (dev @ 4e69171d), 47 exports, 13 logical sections.

## Problem statement

`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` exceeds the 1,000-line maintainability ceiling adopted for
WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 (downtime-worker.ts decomposition). It concentrates
multiple concerns in one module — data types, worklog-dir/CLI-argument
primitives, the bounded-spawn concurrency limiter, JSON extraction, CLI
execution with timeout/retry/in-flight memo, in-process SQLite reads, the
consolidated worklist bundle, critical-child root substitution, review-queue
state, the public fetch API and work-item claiming — making navigation, review
and safe change harder than it needs to be.

## Goal

Break the file into cohesive modules so no file exceeds 1,000 lines.
Producer directive (WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 intake Q1, answered): every source
file over 1,000 lines should be evaluated for refactoring and, where
appropriate, decomposed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No file exceeds 1,000 lines.** After the change, `wc -l` reports ≤1,000 for
   `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` (now a thin barrel) and for every
   `packages/herdr/src/fetcher*.ts` module created by the split.
2. **Public surface preserved.** Every symbol currently imported from
   `./fetcher.js` by another module remains exported from that exact path with
   identical types and values, so the 68 importing files compile with no
   import-path edits. The frozen surface is the **42 consumer-imported symbols**
   captured in `fetcher.split-baseline.json`.
3. **Behaviour-preserving, move-only refactor.** No functional or logic change;
   no test file is modified (not its import paths, fixtures or assertions), and
   all 52 `fetcher`-related test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite
   pass unchanged.
4. **No new circular imports.** Extracted modules import only from concrete
   sibling modules, never from the `./fetcher.js` barrel; the dependency check
   reports no new cycle member and no new runtime cycle.
5. **Module responsibilities documented; full suite green.** Every module has a
   one-line doc comment naming its single responsibility, the herdr docs carry
   a module-layout table, and the full project test suite passes.

## Target module map

| Module | Est. lines | Single responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `fetcher.types.ts` | ~250 | Pure data types (`WorkItem`, `BlockerRef`, `ReviewQueueState`, …) |
| `fetcher.args.ts` | ~140 | Worklog-dir, `wl`-argument and exec-seam primitives |
| `fetcher.spawn-cap.ts` | ~123 | Bounded `wl` spawn concurrency limiter |
| `fetcher.json.ts` | ~142 | `wl`-payload JSON extraction and normalisation |
| `fetcher.cli.ts` | ~280 | `wl` CLI execution: spawn, timeout, retry, in-flight memo |
| `fetcher.inprocess.ts` | ~299 | In-process SQLite read path (fail-open) |
| `fetcher.worklist-bundle.ts` | ~140 | Consolidated `wl worklist` bundle read + snapshot cache |
| `fetcher.review-queue.ts` | ~120 | Review-queue state derivation and query |
| `fetcher.root-substitution.ts` | ~250 | Critical-child root-ancestor substitution + merge tail |
| `fetcher.api.ts` | ~700 | Public fetch API (next, stage, details, deps, children, …) |
| `fetcher.claim.ts` | ~229 | Claim / rollback / needs-producer-review mutations |
| `fetcher.ts` | ≤250 | Thin barrel: doc comment + re-exports only |

## Child decomposition (test-first dependency chain)

1. **Fetcher split guard: freeze surface, ceiling and dependency direction** — test-first gate; no production moves.
2. **Extract fetcher types and arg/exec primitives** — `fetcher.types.ts`, `fetcher.args.ts`.
3. **Extract fetcher spawn-cap and JSON helpers** — `fetcher.spawn-cap.ts`, `fetcher.json.ts`.
4. **Extract fetcher CLI execution and in-process reads** — `fetcher.cli.ts`, `fetcher.inprocess.ts`.
5. **Extract fetcher worklist bundle and review-queue state** — `fetcher.worklist-bundle.ts`, `fetcher.review-queue.ts`.
6. **Extract fetcher root substitution and public fetch API** — `fetcher.root-substitution.ts`, `fetcher.api.ts`.
7. **Extract fetcher work-item claiming** — `fetcher.claim.ts`.
8. **Finalise fetcher barrel, docs and close-out** — thin barrel, empty allowlist, docs, evidence.

Dependency chain: 1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8 (serial; each child is a
complete end-to-end slice: move modules → re-export from the barrel → run the
guard + changed-scope tests).

## Facts captured at plan time (dev @ 4e69171d)

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` = **2,365 lines** (the original description's
  1,579 was stale), **47 exports**, 13 logical sections.
- **68 consumer files** import from `./fetcher.js`: 16 production
  (`index.ts`, `hydrator.ts`, `worklist.ts`, `smart-selection.ts`,
  `index.claim.ts`, `index.downtime-resolvers.ts`, `worklist.detail.ts`,
  `worklist.state.ts`, `dispatch-view.ts`, `visibility.ts`, `code-freeze.ts`,
  `agent-tracker.ts`, `index.interactive.ts`, `index.settings.ts`,
  `md-note-edit.ts`, `worklist.meta.ts`) + 52 test files.
- **42 distinct symbols** are imported by consumers — the frozen public surface.
- Reusable split-guard machinery already exists at
  `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` (with `index-family.ts` and
  `worklist-family.ts` as family precedents).

## Effort / risk

Effort **Medium**, risk **High** — calibrated against the sibling decomposition
epics (index.ts 2,940 lines → Medium/High; worklist.ts 7,899 → Large/High;
sync.ts → Medium/High; interview.ts → Small/Medium). A move-only refactor of a
core module with 68 consumers carries real regression risk even with a guard
test; the guard child is the primary mitigation.

## Related work

- WL-0MVF3F9A7000HKP7 — downtime-worker.ts god class (parent refactor series; completed)
- WL-0MSGAEPOJ002824S — in-process memoization (completed)
- WL-0MVGKGD2Y0038S6B — worklist.ts decomposition (sibling; completed)
- WL-0MVGKGFFN009UCM6 — index.ts decomposition (sibling; completed)
- WL-0MVGKGMU400631VZ — src/sync.ts decomposition (sibling; completed)
- WL-0MVV3NB39001DG8J — worklist split guard (related guard precedent)

# Maintenance routines skill: create/maintain daily scheduled test, standup, refactor sessions at high priority

## Headline

A new ContextHub skill (`/skill:maintenance-routines`) that creates and maintains the required daily scheduled maintenance sessions (test 07:00, standup 08:00, refactor 09:00) in each project's `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatching all of them at **high request priority** so they are processed even in peak periods — backed by a herdr enhancement that threads a per-entry `priority` (default `high`) into the `X-Priority` request header.

## Problem statement

Every project should run regular automated maintenance routines (test suite, standup report, refactor pass). The herdr plugin already has the mechanism (`scheduled-prompts.json`, dispatched on idle by the downtime worker), but there is no maintained, canonical set: the current template/live config only carries `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (06:05, no priority), and **no** `/skill:test` routine. Worse, dispatched scheduled prompts have no work item, so they receive the downtime request-priority default `medium` (`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium`) — they can be starved behind peak-period contention. The operator wants the three routines scheduled daily (07:00/08:00/09:00) and dispatched at **high** priority.

## Users

- **Project operator** — wants the three routines to reliably exist in each project's schedule and to be processed even in peak periods.
- **Automated maintenance sessions** (`/skill:test`, `/skill:standup`, `/skill:refactor`) — must carry `X-Priority: high` on every provider request so `llama-proxy` serves them ahead of the contention queue.

### Example user stories

- As an operator, I run `/skill:maintenance-routines` on a project and it ensures `/skill:test` (daily 07:00), `/skill:standup` (daily 08:00) and `/skill:refactor` (daily 09:00) are present and correctly configured in `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, without touching my last-run timestamps or any custom entries.
- As an operator, I know every scheduled maintenance session is dispatched with `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=high` (→ `X-Priority: high`), so the daily test/standup/refactor runs are served even during peak periods.
- As an operator, when I provision a new project with `wl init`, it comes pre-loaded with the same three routines (daily, timed, high priority).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Skill exists and reconciles the schedule.** `skill/maintenance-routines/` ships a `SKILL.md`, a reconciler script and unit tests. Invoking it (or the script directly) reconciles the project-local `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (under the resolved worklog dir) so these required routines are present and exact:
   - `/skill:test` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "07:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:standup` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "08:00"`, `priority: "high"`
   - `/skill:refactor` — `intervalDays: 1`, `time: "09:00"`, `priority: "high"`
2. **Reconcile is non-destructive and idempotent.** Entries are created if absent; drifted fields (interval/time/priority) are corrected; `lastTriggeredAt` and all other user-defined entries are preserved verbatim; a second run makes no further changes; missing or malformed config files are handled fail-closed with a clear report; `--dry-run` shows the planned diff without writing.
3. **Herdr honours a per-entry `priority` field.** `ScheduledPrompt` gains an optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`) validated in `parseScheduledPrompt` (invalid value → entry skipped with a warning, fail-closed); **absent → defaults to `high`** for scheduled prompts. The scheduled-prompt dispatch passes it through `spawnAgentPane({ priority })` → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` → `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (so `high` → `X-Priority: high` on every request). Unit tests cover parse defaults/validation and the dispatch threading.
4. **Template provisions the required set.** `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set) is updated to the three required routines with daily `intervalDays`, `time` and `priority: high`, so new projects are provisioned with the routines (create-if-absent semantics unchanged — existing configs are never clobbered).
5. **Documentation criterion.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (Scheduled prompts section), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (Request priority section) and `CONFIG.md` (Scheduled-prompts config section) document the new `priority` field, the default-`high` behaviour, and the three routines; the maintenance-routines skill is referenced from the relevant skill docs listing.
6. **Testing criterion.** Skill tests (`pytest` under `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/`) cover reconcile/idempotence/preservation/dry-run; herdr unit tests (`vitest`) cover the new parse/validation and dispatch priority; full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No changes to the interactive dispatch path or to the other downtime tiers' mapping tables** (`request-priority.ts` stays fixed); only the scheduled-prompt entry schema, its dispatch call, and the skill/template change.
- The requested **default is `high`** for scheduled prompts (operator decision Q1): an entry that wants lower priority must set the field explicitly (`low`/`medium`). This is a deliberate change from the current downtime default (`medium`) for scheduled prompts only.
- No code-behaviour changes to `wl init` — only the **contents** of `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the provisioning path and create-if-absent semantics stay as-is).
- The skill must be safe to run from any project root (`wl`-independent — it reads/writes only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`, atomic tmp+rename, matching herdr's `saveScheduledPrompts` pattern).

## Existing state

- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (and the live `/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`) currently carry only `/skill:refactor` (3-day interval, no time) and `/skill:standup` (daily `time: "06:05"`); no `/skill:test`; no priority field anywhere.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — schema (`id|prompt|intervalDays|lastTriggeredAt|time?`), fail-closed parse, due-check, atomic persist; **no priority support**.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` calls `spawnAgentPane(prompt.prompt, { model, cwd, paneName, anchorId })` with **no priority** → `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions({ priority: undefined })` → `mapDowntimeRequestPriority(undefined)` → `medium` (docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md, "Scheduled prompts have no work item and get the downtime default (medium)").
- `src/commands/init.ts` — `ensureScheduledPromptsInstalled` copies the template create-if-absent; unchanged in behaviour.
- Skills precedent: `skill/heartbeat/` and `skill/pane-triage/` (SKILL.md + scripts + tests, tracked in ContextHub, deployed to `~/.pi/agent/skills/<name>`); shared helpers in `skill/shared/`.

## Desired change

1. **New skill** `skill/maintenance-routines/`: `SKILL.md` (spec: required-routines table, invocation, admission of a bootstrap `/skill:maintenance-routines` schedule), `scripts/maintenance_routines.py` (reconcile + `--dry-run`; atomic writes; preserves `lastTriggeredAt` and foreign entries), `tests/` (unit tests).

5. **Tests**: pytest for the skill reconciler; vitest for parse/validation + dispatch threading in herdr.

## Key Files

- `skill/maintenance-routines/SKILL.md` — new skill spec (required-routines table, usage, dry-run).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/scripts/maintenance_routines.py` — new reconciler CLI (`--dry-run`, atomic write, preserves state).
- `skill/maintenance-routines/tests/test_maintenance_routines.py` — new unit tests (reconcile, idempotence, preservation, malformed config, dry-run).
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.ts` — add optional `priority` (`low|medium|high|critical`, default `high`), validation in `parseScheduledPrompt`.
- `packages/herdr/src/scheduled-prompts.test.ts` — new parse/default/validation cases.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `dispatchScheduledPrompt` passes `prompt.priority` to `spawnAgentPane`.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (or the scheduled-prompts tier test) — dispatch threads `priority: 'high'` into the spawn opts/env.
- `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` — updated to the three required routines.
- `packages/herdr/README.md`, `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `CONFIG.md` — document the new field/default and the routines.
- `tests/skill/maintenance-routines/` — integration-style tests for the skill (repo test-suite convention, cf. `tests/skill/heartbeat/`).

## Related work

- **WL-0MSS1Q5ER007QDKX** (completed) — herdr downtime dispatcher: scheduled prompts (best-effort frequency) config — the mechanism the skill maintains.
- **WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH / WL-0MVF3Q3VL000UNCN** (completed) — request priority (`X-Priority`) mapping tables and `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` env threading — the priority plumbing we reuse.
- **WL-0MTF5UAJ4000LLZ9** (completed) — removal of scheduled-prompts console output (no-op here).
- **WL-0MUKYERLZ006ELL5** (completed) — non-terminal cooldown for dispatched panes (context for scheduled dispatch behaviour).
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** (completed) — periodic request scheduling to the pi worklog plugin; the scheduled-prompts feature parent.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRHYQU1S009DJ9B** – Add periodic request scheduling to pi worklog plugin (completed)
- **WL-0MTMN7W63001FCQR** – Scheduled prompts: add time-of-day dispatch (time window) to scheduled-prompts tier (completed)

- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: convey, create, creates, currently, daily (+26 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: create, creates, daily, default, dispatched (+25 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — default-`high` changes politeness of ALL scheduled prompts** (including custom future entries). Accepted by operator (Q1: "default high"); any entry can opt down via an explicit `low`/`medium` field. Mitigation: document prominently.
- **Risk — parse strictness.** An invalid `priority` value rejects the whole entry (consistent with existing `time` handling) — a config typo could silently disable a routine. Mitigation: the skill always writes a valid value; tests cover the failure path.
- **Risk — skill/template drift.** If `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` is later edited, the skill's required table may diverge. Mitigation: keep the required-routines table in one place (the skill), and the template mirrors it (as Q3).
- **Assumption — the skill runs per project root.** Invoked via a pi session (herdr pane or manual) with `cwd` at the project root; it reads/writes only `<cwd>/.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json` (worklog-dir safe).
- **Assumption — operators may bootstrap the skill itself as a scheduled prompt** (e.g. daily `/skill:maintenance-routines`) to keep the schedule self-healing; not required for this item.
- **Scope-creep guard:** no changes to interactive dispatch, `request-priority.ts` tables, other downtime tiers, or `wl init` code; any opportunity discovered during implementation is recorded as a new linked work item, not added here.

- **Q1: How should scheduled routines get high priority?**

  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): "1. A (default high)"** — per-entry field; **absent → default `high`**.
  - Reasoning recorded: matches "all those work items should be sent high priority so they get processed even in peak periods"; keeps intent in the config; future entries can opt down explicitly.
- **Q2: How strictly should the skill maintain the required set?**
  - Options: (a) ensure the three required routines exist & match spec (create-if-absent, fix drifted fields), keep other user entries; (b) strict whitelist (remove anything else); (c) create-if-absent only (never fix drift).
  - **Answer (producer): "2. A"** — non-destructive reconcile, preserve custom entries.
- **Q3: Should new projects get the routines by default?**
  - Options: (a) also update `templates/scheduled-prompts.json` (the `wl init` base set); (b) skill-only.
  - **Answer (producer): "3. A"** — template updated so every new project provisions the three routines at 07:00/08:00/09:00 high (`wl init` code path unchanged).

# Canonical full suite excludes `packages/` tests (tui 30 + shared 13 files)

*Discovered from WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR (canonical suite root-level `tests/` coverage).* That item closed the `tests/` gap by replacing the two narrow `suiteCommands` with the umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`. It deliberately kept its scope to `tests/`, so the `packages/` gap remains.

**Note:** file counts have grown since the work item was created — `packages/tui` now has 30 test files (was 22) and `packages/shared` has 13 (was 12). The `packages/herdr` count is 129, unchanged. Repository total: 453 test files (up from 440).

## Problem Statement

`.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` (the single source of full-suite evidence for `/skill:test --type full`, the ship release gate and audit F3) resolves only to `tests/`. Tracked test files by location:

| Location | Test files | In canonical suite? |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/` | 277 | Yes (since WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR) |
| `packages/herdr` | 129 | No — producer decision (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); opt-in `--type herdr` / `--group herdr` |
| `packages/tui` | 30 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| `packages/shared` | 13 | **No — no coverage anywhere** |
| **Repository total** | **453** | **277** |

`packages/tui/**/*.test.ts` (30 files, all under `packages/tui/extensions/`) and `packages/shared/**/*.test.ts` (13 files) run under a bare `npx vitest` / CI but are referenced by neither `suiteCommands` nor any cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths, so no gate can execute or cache-evidence them. (Note: a `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`.)

## Goal

Every `packages/` test file is either executed by the canonical full suite (or a cache-recorded group that gates the corresponding paths), or has an explicit documented exclusion with a rationale — the same standard WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR applied to `tests/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `.pi/test-config.json` covers `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` tests (in `suiteCommands`, or as named `groups` entries wired to their paths so `implement.py finish` selects them), or each exclusion is documented with a rationale in `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md`.
- A full `/skill:test` run (`python3 <test-skill>/scripts/run_tests.py --type full --json`) reports the newly covered files as executed, with the executed-file count recorded in the work item.
- Any failures surfaced by the change are triaged into `test-failure` work items.
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` (the "Test gates" section is shared, not duplicated) carries the updated coverage table (files executed / excluded / why) and the measured runtime.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Evidence-path constraint:** full-suite evidence for the audit resolves `--type full` from `suiteCommands` only; a new `groups.*` entry alone does not satisfy a "full suite passes" AC (see `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` → "Cache evidence scope").
- **Vitest filters are substring matches** on the repository-relative path, so `packages/shared` / `packages/tui` can be selected by positional filters (`-- tests` umbrella does not cover them; `-- packages` would also pull in `packages/herdr`, which is excluded by producer decision).
- **Do not re-litigate the herdr decision** (WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix; `groups.herdr` added by WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN).
- Measure runtime before/after with the test-skill runner (`run_tests.py`), not ad-hoc `npx vitest`.
- Beware the `run_tests.py --suite node` trap: that suite name resolves through the legacy convention path (`tests/{unit,node,cli}`) and ignores `suiteCommands`; use the default `--suite all` for canonical runs.

## Existing state

The canonical suite is a single command: `npm --silent test -- tests` (277 files, ~791 s vitest duration, ~1065 s wall clock). The `tui-extensions` group exists in `groups` but is not wired into `suiteCommands`. There is no group for `packages/shared`.

## Desired change

Add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to the canonical full suite coverage. The simplest approach is to add additional commands to `suiteCommands`:

```jsonc
{
  "suiteCommands": [
    "npm --silent test -- tests",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/shared",
    "npm --silent test -- packages/tui/extensions"
  ]
}
```

This adds two positional filters that are precise: `packages/shared` matches only the 13 shared test files, and `packages/tui/extensions` matches only the 30 tui test files (all under `extensions/`), neither of which would match `packages/herdr`.

Alternatively, create named groups (`shared`, `tui`) and wire them into `suiteCommands` as separate commands — same effect, but with changed-scope selection benefits.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `.pi/test-config.json` — add `packages/shared` and `packages/tui` to `suiteCommands` (or create named groups + wire them)
- `docs/dev/test-suite-baseline.md` — update the coverage table and runtime section
- `vitest.config.ts` — no change expected; existing config handles `packages/` correctly

## Related work

- **WL-0MVG4FF9200346NR** — closed the `tests/` coverage gap (umbrella `npm --silent test -- tests`); records the OPEN QUESTION that became this item.
- **WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8** — herdr package suite excluded by producer decision (won't-fix).
- **WL-0MVH751AJ009R4SN** — added `groups.herdr` to `.pi/test-config.json`.
- **WL-0MVNUHWH500196K1** — source of the additional-gap evidence for `packages/tui/extensions/**`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should packages/herdr be included?" — Answer (work item description): No — producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8, closed won't-fix. Source: work item description.
- Q: "What about the `tui-extensions` group that already exists?" — Answer: It is not wired into `suiteCommands`, so it provides no full-suite gate coverage. The brief proposes wiring it (or creating an equivalent group) into suiteCommands. Source: inspection of `.pi/test-config.json`.
- Q: "File counts have changed since the work item was created — should we update the title?" — Answer: Yes — the title should be updated to reflect current counts (30 + 13, not 22 + 12). Source: `git ls-files` on current tree.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Runtime increase (medium).** Adding 43 files to the canonical suite increases wall-clock. *Mitigation:* measure before/after with `run_tests.py`; `timeoutPerCommand` is 3600 s, so there is headroom.
- **New coverage may surface pre-existing failures (medium).** Neither `packages/tui` nor `packages/shared` has run under the canonical gate, so latent failures could appear. *Mitigation:* triage into `test-failure` items (AC3).
- **Filter precision (low).** `packages/shared` and `packages/tui/extensions` are substring filters; verified against `git ls-files` that they match only the intended 13 + 30 files and not `packages/herdr`. *Assumption:* `packages/tui` has no test files outside `extensions/` (confirmed: 30/30 are under `extensions/`).
- **Scope creep (low).** `packages/herdr` is explicitly out of scope (producer decision WL-0MVFZVIA50062TJ8); covering it would require re-litigating a closed won't-fix decision. Any further gap (e.g. a new package) becomes a linked work item, not added scope.
- **Assumption:** adding commands to `suiteCommands` (rather than only `groups`) is required, because `--type full` evidence resolves from `suiteCommands` only (evidence-path constraint). A group-only change would not satisfy AC2.

Fix stale packages/herdr/package-lock.json drift that fails the test-skill live-repo guard

Discovered during WL-0MVOBP6K0007574C (extract dependency and comment modules).

## Problem

`packages/herdr/package.json` declares a root `bin` entry
(`worklog-pane-close` -> `dist/pane-close-cli.js`) and a `postinstall` script,
but the committed `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` (last touched
2026-08-11, WL-0MSNULGSM00018I4) predates both. Any `npm ci`/`npm install` in
that package rewrites the lockfile with `hasInstallScript: true` and the root
`bin` block.

`tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` executes `scripts/install-herdr.sh`
(cwd = repo root), which runs `npm ci` inside `packages/herdr`. The rewritten
lockfile is therefore a mutation of a guarded checkout made during a test run,
so the test skill's live-repo guard fails the run:

```
live-repo mutation detected: the test suite changed a guarded checkout for <repo>.
  added path [ M] packages/herdr/package-lock.json
```

Every test in the suite passes (281 files / 4,113 tests, exit 0) — only the run
verdict is failed. Consequences:

- The per-repo test cache can never hold a green full-suite entry for HEAD, so
  the audit skill cannot auto-verify execution-dependent ACs (F3 re-executes and
  fails the same way).
- Each full-suite run leaves the main checkout dirty.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `packages/herdr/package-lock.json` is regenerated (`npm install` in
   `packages/herdr`) and committed so it matches `package.json`'s `bin` and
   `postinstall`.
2. A full-suite run (`run_tests.py --scope full`) at that commit reports
   `success: true` with no `live_repo_mutation` field, and leaves
   `git status` clean.
3. `npm run build` and `npm ci` in `packages/herdr` produce no further lockfile
   diff.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/package-lock.json`
- `packages/herdr/package.json` — read-only
- `tests/scripts/install-herdr.test.ts` — read-only (reproduction)

## Constraint

Lockfile-only change; do not alter `package.json` or the install script.

# Make groupings stable

## Problem statement

When the herdr selection list re-sorts on refresh, items sometimes move from
one group to another even though nothing about them changed materially. This
causes disconcerting movement in the list. The list should only change when
the underlying items change in a material way (e.g. a new key file is added,
or the priority changes). Additionally, items should sort in priority order —
all high items ahead of medium, all medium ahead of low.

## Users

- **Herdr users / producers** who watch the worklist to decide what to work
  on next. A stable list lets them track where work sits; gratuitous movement
  breaks their mental model of the queue.
- **Producers reviewing the in-review queue** who rely on a predictable
  within-group order to find the most important work first.

User story: *As a Herdr user, I want the worklist grouping and ordering to be
a stable function of the items themselves, so that an item only changes
group when its content (key files, priority, stage/status) or the item set
changes — and within each group, high-priority items always rank above
medium, which rank above low.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Group assignment is **content-deterministic**: for a fixed set of items
      with fixed key files / priority / stage / status, the group each item
      lands in is identical regardless of the order in which the items are
      presented to the grouping algorithm (canonical ordering applied before
      the greedy first-fit packing). A transient change such as an
      `updatedAt` timestamp (comment added, audit run) must never change an
      item's group.
- [ ] An item's group membership changes **only** when a material input
      changes: its key files section, its priority, its stage/status, or the
      item set itself (item added/removed). Verified by a stability test
      that perturbs non-material inputs (`updatedAt`, input order) and
      asserts group labels/numbers are unchanged.
- [ ] Within each group (Critical Group N and Group N), items sort by
      **priority first (high → medium → low)**, then by the existing stage
      sub-order (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then by
      id — so all high items appear ahead of all medium items, which appear
      ahead of all low items. The `in_review` 6-bucket comparator already
      sorts priority-first and keeps that behaviour.
- [ ] The change is applied **and kept in sync** in both mirrors: core
      `wl next` / `wl worklist` grouping (`src/commands/grouping.ts`,
      `src/worklist-selection.ts`) and the herdr plugin copy
      (`packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`); shared grouping tests cover both
      copies.
- [ ] `wl next -n N` and the herdr worklist still emit the canonical section
      order (Critical Group N → Group N → Idea → Other → In Review) with no
      regression in existing grouping/smart-selection behaviour.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes; all related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
      comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Greedy first-fit file-path conflict detection is retained — the change
  makes it order-independent, it does not replace the packing strategy.
- Herdr plugin has zero npm dependencies and cannot import from
  `src/commands/`; the mirror must stay a self-contained pure duplication
  (per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B decision Q2c).
- The always-show-mandatory guarantee of `selectWorkItems`
  (`packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts`) is preserved — grouping only
  reorders and stamps, never filters or drops items.
- Default `maxGroups` of 3 for file-path-based groups is unchanged.

## Existing state

- `regroupWorkItems` (herdr) / `selectBrowseFeed` (core) recompute group
  assignments on every refresh from the merged selection.
- `groupItemsByFilePaths` is a greedy first-fit over items **in input
  order**; the input order fluctuates with `updatedAt` (comment/audit
  churn), so the same item set can pack into different groups across
  refreshes. That is the root cause of the observed group hopping.
- Within-group ordering (`compareGroupableItems`) currently sorts by stage
  sub-order first (`plan_complete` → `intake_complete` → remaining), then
  priority; `in_review` items already sort priority-first.

## Desired change

1. Make `groupItemsByFilePaths` (and hence `assignItemGroups`) a pure
   function of the item content: sort/canonicalise the input items by a
   stable content-derived key before greedy packing, so group membership
   depends only on ids, key files, priority and stage/status — not on
   transient ordering.
2. Make priority the **primary** within-group sort key in
   `compareGroupableItems` (both mirrors), keeping the stage sub-order as
   the secondary key.
3. Keep the two mirrors in sync and extend the grouping tests in both
   locations with stability assertions (order perturbation + non-material
   input perturbation must not change group membership or ordering).

## Key Files

- `src/commands/grouping.ts` — core `groupItemsByFilePaths` / `assignItemGroups` / `compareGroupableItems`; canonicalise input order; priority-first within-group sort.
- `src/worklist-selection.ts` — core `selectBrowseFeed` grouping pipeline consuming `assignItemGroups`.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — mirrored plugin copy of the same algorithm; must stay in sync.
- `packages/herdr/src/smart-selection.ts` — `selectWorkItems`; input order source feeding `regroupWorkItems` (contract only — no functional change expected unless needed for canonicalisation).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.api.ts` / `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.root-substitution.ts` — callers of `regroupWorkItems`.
- `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` — core grouping tests; add stability assertions.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.test.ts` — plugin grouping tests; mirror stability assertions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Within-group order change is intentional but observable:** making priority
  the primary within-group sort key changes which item of a group renders
  first (stage sub-order becomes secondary). Existing tests in
  `grouping.test.ts` / `tests/grouping-utility.test.ts` that assert the old
  stage-first order must be updated deliberately, not incidentally.
- **Canonicalisation key must be content-derived:** the pre-pack sort key
  (e.g. priority + stage + id) must never include timestamps or insertion
  order, or the instability simply moves to the new key.
- **Assumption — "material change" definition:** key files (the `**Key Files:**`
  section), priority, stage/status, or item-set membership. Description prose
  outside the Key Files section already cannot affect grouping
  (`extractFilePaths` reads only that section) and stays non-material.
- **Scope-creep guard:** out-of-scope opportunities (stable group *labels*
  across renumbering, configurable `maxGroups`) are recorded as related/future
  work, not implemented here.

## Related work

- WL-0MSAKPVR9005B6XJ — Rewrite `assignItemGroups` + `next.ts` ordering (completed; produced the current grouping spec this item stabilises).
- WL-0MSAK8YLB0025EGW — Herdr plugin: fix work item list grouping (duplicate In Review sections, wrong group order) (completed; established section order + `regroupWorkItems`).
- WL-0MUY1CSQG007TCYX — actively-worked items derived from `status === 'in-progress'` (affects group membership inputs).
- WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G — in_review priority-first ordering (precedent for priority-first within-group sort).

### Related work (automated report)

Low-relevance automatic matches (find-related): WL-0MR1COW20005IO1C (Bubble
up critical items), WL-0MRSGMTYY0062WFJ (audit-set fail hard), WL-0MLGTWT4S1X4HDD9
(needs-producer-review filter) — adjacent selection-list behaviour, no AC
overlap with this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should priority ordering apply? (A) within each group only, (B) globally across the whole list, (C) both" — Answer (producer): **A — within each group only**. Source: interactive reply (intake round, recommended option accepted).
- Q2: "Stability definition — (A) content-deterministic grouping via canonical sort before fit, (B) keep packing, only stabilise within-group ordering" — Answer (producer): **A — content-deterministic grouping**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted).
- Q3: "Scope of the change — (A) both mirrors kept in sync, (B) herdr only, (C) core only" — Answer (producer): **A — both, kept in sync**. Source: interactive reply (recommended option accepted). Research: confirmed the duplicate lives at `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` per WL-0MS8W5LTW006YZ4B Q2c.
data.title: Make groupings stable

# Remove the heartbeat skill (superseded by the downtime dispatcher)

## Problem statement

The `heartbeat` skill (`/skill:heartbeat`) predates the herdr downtime dispatcher and duplicates — while contradicting — it. It is not in use: no invocation appears anywhere in the Pi session archive, and nothing in `wl`, the herdr plugin, cron, systemd or the test suite calls it. Keeping it costs two drifted copies of the same script that must both be maintained, plus a second, off-contract work-item ranking path.

## Evidence gathered (2026-10-30)

**No usage:**

- `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: zero occurrences of `/skill:heartbeat` as a user prompt (`"text":"/skill:heartbeat"` → 0 files); the ~1,000 hits are the skill-catalogue description embedded in every system prompt.
- No tool-result output of a real run (`"Flagged … for producer review"`, `"No items in completed/in_review queue"`) anywhere in the archive — those strings appear only inside the skill's own source/SKILL.md text.
- No crontab entry, no systemd timer, no herdr plugin hook, no caller in `packages/herdr/src` (the only "heartbeat" hits there are the unrelated *sync* heartbeat), no reference from any other skill.

**Superseded by the downtime dispatcher** (`docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`):

| | `heartbeat` skill | Downtime dispatcher |
|---|---|---|
| Trigger | manual `/skill:heartbeat`, one action per call | continuous, leader-elected idle dispatch |
| Audit invocation | headless `pi -p --mode json --no-session /skill:audit <id>`, 600 s timeout, invisible | visible herdr pane, with pane monitor, stall resume and attempt budget |
| Audit threshold | review queue ≥ 10 (hard-coded) | review-queue gate `count >= browseItemCount` (live setting) + depth-aware audit batching |
| Candidate ranking | `wl next` — a **second ranking path** | "dispatcher == Herdr list head"; a second ranking is explicitly disallowed |
| `needsProducerReview` | set as a "look at this next" nudge on a sparse queue | a **dispatch hold**, set only on attempt-budget exhaustion |

**Duplicate drift:** `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` (resolved at runtime) and `skill/heartbeat/` (imported by the tests) are separate git-tracked copies that have diverged in their audit dispatch (`pi -p` vs `audit_runner.py`); the parity guard in `tests/skill/heartbeat/test_heartbeat.py` exists only to stop further divergence. Removal eliminates the drift by construction.

**Deliberate coverage loss:** automated audit dispatch without herdr. The dispatcher lives in the herdr plugin and requires idle local-LLM capacity; a herdr-less mode would need a new implementation against the dispatcher's contract. Accepted — there is no herdr-less deployment today.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `skill/heartbeat/` and `.pi/skills/heartbeat/` are removed from the repository, so `/skill:heartbeat` no longer resolves in Pi and no duplicate copy remains.
2. `tests/skill/heartbeat/` (unit and integration suites) is removed; no test imports or references the heartbeat module.
3. The `README.md` feature blurb and the docs table row advertising the heartbeat skill are removed.

The superseded work items recorded as deleted with the dispatcher named as the replacement: heartbeat audit notifications (WL-0MSG5THFC004WJEI) and the `.pi` copy-drift item (WL-0MVVM0SLV0053QP8). *(Both were soft-deleted at filing time; this AC needs no implementation work — verify only that nothing still references them.)*

# Manually created tabs go to the left, dispatched tabs to the right

## Problem statement

Tabs spawned by the operator from the Herdr Worklog selection list (e.g. `p` for plan, `i` for implement, `p-n` for a new pi session, or any other ID-carrying interactive dispatch) currently append at the **right** end of the workspace tab row, away from the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab they belong next to. Automated dispatch tabs (downtime dispatcher) append there too. Operator-created tabs should instead land immediately to the **left** of the Worklog/extensions tab, while automated dispatches keep today's right-side placement.

## Users

- The operator (producer/developer) driving work out of the Herdr Worklog selection list. Example user stories:
  - "As an operator, when I hit `i` to implement a work item, I want the new item tab to appear next to the Worklog tab so my manually opened sessions stay grouped and my work-in-progress tabs don't get pushed out of view at the far right of the tab row."
  - "As an operator, when I open a new pi session from the selection list, I want it beside the other manually opened sessions rather than at the end of a long tab row."

## Acceptance Criteria

- An interactive dispatch that **creates a new tab** (ID-carrying commands such as `/skill:*`, `/intake`, `/plan`, prompt/`!!`/`!` commands carrying a work-item ID, and a new-pi-session dispatch from the selection list) places that tab immediately to the **left of the Worklog (extensions/plugin) tab** in the invoking workspace.
- Automated dispatches (downtime dispatcher) place their tabs at the default right-side position exactly as today — no behaviour change.
- Tab repositioning is implemented via the herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` set to the extensions tab's index (or an equivalent herdr CLI/socket mechanism available at implement time); the tab is first created as today and then moved.
- Fail-open: when the Worklog/extensions tab cannot be resolved (no plugin pane, no tab labelled `Worklog`, multiple/ambiguous matches) or `tab.move` fails, the newly created tab stays at its default right-side position — the dispatch is never blocked, dropped, or placed in a wrong workspace.
- Reuse semantics are preserved: an **existing** item-ID tab is adopted without being moved (only freshly provisioned tabs are repositioned; a reused tab's position is the operator's own arrangement).
- At least one automated test (unit or integration) covers each of: left placement for an interactively created tab, default right placement for a dispatcher-created tab, and fail-open when the extensions tab or the move is unavailable.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No herdr core changes in scope: herdr 0.9.5 CLI `tab create` has no insert/position flag — the repositioning must go through the socket API (`tab.move` with `insert_index`) or an existing CLI mechanism, and must tolerate the capability being absent (fail-open).
- The "extensions tab" is the tab hosting the Worklog selection list / plugin TUI — i.e. the tab containing a pane labelled `Work Items` (`PLUGIN_PANE_LABEL`), commonly renamed to `Worklog` by `open-worklog-tab.sh`.
- Interactive and dispatcher callers share the same tab-creation choke points (`createTabInWorkspace`, the anchor resolvers); the change must distinguish the two so only operator-initiated creation repositions.
- Root-pane cleanup semantics (fail-safe liveness check, WS-holder placeholder close) and the fail-open dispatch guarantees from the interactive item-tab work must be preserved.
- Keep changes surgical; do not introduce a second tab mechanism or restructure the dispatcher-adoption logic.

## Existing state

- `herdr tab create` appends a new tab at the right end of the workspace tab row; both the interactive item-ID path and the downtime dispatcher path create tabs this way, so all tabs land to the right of existing tabs.
- Interactive ID-carrying dispatches provision a tab labelled exactly `<itemId>` via `getItemTabAnchor` (`dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts`) — created on first use, adopted thereafter — split via `send-to-pi.sh`/`run-in-pane.sh` with `--anchor`, with fail-safe placeholder root-pane cleanup.
- The downtime dispatcher provisions its own tabs (Dispatcher workspace / project workspace item tabs) through the same herdr CLI tab primitives.
- herdr socket API exposes `tab.move` (with `insert_index`) and emits `tab.moved` events carrying the requested `insert_index` and the updated ordered tab list.

## Desired change

- At the tab-creation choke point, add an interactive-placement mode (e.g. a `placement: 'left-of-extensions'` flag/param, defaulting to today's behaviour) set only by the interactive dispatch path.
- After a freshly provisioned tab is created for an interactive dispatch, resolve the Worklog/extensions tab in that workspace (pane labelled `Work Items`, falling back to a tab labelled `Worklog`) and `tab.move` the new tab to `insert_index` = that tab's index (immediately left of it). Fail-open at every boundary.
- Dispatcher-created tabs, and adopted (reused) interactive tabs, are untouched.

**Key Files:**
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.herdr-cli.ts` — `createTabInWorkspace` (and any new `tab move` CLI/socket helper) — the tab-creation choke point.
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.placement.ts` — `getItemTabAnchor` provisioning path (interactive item-ID tabs).
- `packages/herdr/src/index.interactive.ts` — `resolveInteractiveItemAnchor` / `closeInteractiveTabRootPane` (interactive vs dispatcher call-site split).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.tab-anchors.ts` / `downtime-worker.pane.ts` — dispatcher tab provisioning (must remain right-placed).
- `packages/herdr/src/dispatcher-anchor.contract.ts` — `PLUGIN_PANE_LABEL` (`Work Items`) and any new placement-mode types/labels.
- Tests alongside each module (`*.test.ts`) plus the split-guard baselines if CLI helper signatures change.

## Related work

- WL-0MUYI3JAO002BTNL — "Implement: interactive item-tab placement" (completed) — established the interactive item-ID tab anchor + `--anchor` forwarding this work extends.
- WL-0MUKZGEQ2007FECS — "Pi processes should start in a work item tab" (completed epic) — parent of the interactive placement work.
- WL-0MUYI3K8H007MPKF / WL-0MUYI3JRC006115V — interactive item-tab root-pane cleanup (implement/test).
- WL-0MUYI3KPB0024U86 — "Docs: interactive item-ID-tab placement" (completed) — docs companion to update.
- WL-0MTR01EU7005SYZG — "Downtime dispatch panes all spawn in the leader's workspace…" (completed) — dispatcher anchor-by-ID workspace; the automated path that stays right-placed.
- WL-0MU2EOHK900425VU — "dispatcher workspace has useless pane" (completed) — root-pane cleanup precedent.
- WL-0MVGKHCP9005SJPZ (refactor) — decomposed `dispatcher-anchor.ts`; placement code now lives in the split modules above.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Extensions-tab resolution ambiguity** — if multiple tabs contain a `Work Items`-labelled pane, or both a `Worklog`-labelled tab and a `Work Items` pane tab exist, the anchor choice must be deterministic; fail-open (leave tab right) on none/ambiguous rather than misplace.
- **herdr `tab.move` availability** — depends on the socket API of the running herdr (0.9.5 supports it); if absent or failing, the tab stays where created (right) — never block the dispatch.
- **Created-vs-reused signal** — repositioning must apply only to freshly provisioned tabs; reusing the existing `onCreate` create-vs-reuse observer avoids disturbing tabs the operator arranged manually.
- **Scope-creep risk** — reordering existing/adopted tabs, changing dispatcher (right) placement, or reworking the pane-splitting (non-tab) interactive paths are out of scope; record any such follow-up as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption: keybinding coverage** — `p`/`i`/`p-n` and other interactive dispatches resolve to the interactive `onCommand` path (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts`); treat any interactive dispatch that creates a tab as operator-created. Non-tab (current-pane split) routes are unaffected.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What is 'the extensions tab'?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "(a) The tab hosting the Worklog selection list / plugin TUI (currently renamed 'Worklog')." Source: interactive reply, this intake session (WL-0MVZ88G51004IYHW).
- Q2: "Acceptable implementation mechanism (herdr 0.9.5 CLI `tab create` has no insert flag)?" — Answer (operator): "(a) create the tab as today, then reposition via herdr socket API `tab.move` with `insert_index` = index of the extensions tab." Source: interactive reply.
- Q3: "Which interactions count as operator-created, and where should the change live?" — Answer (operator): "(a) All interactive dispatch paths — item-ID tabs from `p`/`i`/other ID-carrying commands AND `p-n` new-pi-session tabs — moved left, applied in `packages/herdr` tab-creation code (`createTabInWorkspace`/anchor resolvers)." Source: interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKVZ3RBL10DFPPW** – Use Alt+Right Arrow to advance focus (replace Tab) (completed)
- **WL-0MTRQT482001SNXC** – Downtime dispatcher: per-project tabs in Dispatcher workspace (route each prefix to its own tab) (completed)
- **WL-0MSKUAT5D00443GA** – Impl: tab-focus-gated visibility in visibility.ts + docs (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: automated, created, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, manually, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: automated, created, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, manually, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: automated, dispatcher, downtime, extensions, herdr, implement, left, list, need, new, now, operator, place, plan, processes, right, selection, session, spawning, tab, tabs, they, when

# Fetcher split guard: freeze surface, ceiling and dependency direction

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Source:** `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` = 2,365 lines, 47 exports, 13 sections (dev @ 4e69171d)

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `fetcher.ts` split, I want one automated gate that
fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so that every
extraction child can land safely without touching any existing test file and
without a reviewer having to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1–AC4 require: every production module ≤1,000 lines, an unchanged
public surface at `./fetcher.js`, unmodified test files, and no new circular
imports. Nothing in the repo enforces these for `fetcher.ts` today.

The `downtime-worker`, `worklist` and `index` decompositions already built this
machinery: `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` exports the generic
predicates (`loadModuleIndex`, `consumerImportNames`, `findMissingExports`,
`resolveImportTarget`, `isTypeOnlyImport`, `findCycleBaselineViolations`,
`findOversizedModules`, `findAllowlistViolations`, …) and each family adds a
thin `<family>-family.ts` config module. **Reuse `scan.ts` unchanged; never edit
it** — this child adds only the fetcher-specific gaps.

Facts captured at plan time (dev @ 4e69171d, `packages/herdr`):

- **2,365 lines**, 47 exports, 13 logical sections.
- **68 consumer files** import from `./fetcher.js`: 16 production
  (`index.ts`, `hydrator.ts`, `worklist.ts`, `smart-selection.ts`,
  `index.claim.ts`, `index.downtime-resolvers.ts`, `worklist.detail.ts`,
  `worklist.state.ts`, `dispatch-view.ts`, `visibility.ts`, `code-freeze.ts`,
  `agent-tracker.ts`, `index.interactive.ts`, `index.settings.ts`,
  `md-note-edit.ts`, `worklist.meta.ts`) + 52 test files.
- **42 distinct symbols** are imported by consumers — the frozen surface:
  `BlockerRef`, `DEFAULT_WL_SPAWN_CAP`, `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WorkItem`,
  `_resetWlSpawnStats`, `_wlSpawnStats`, `buildWlArgs`, `buildWlArgsForRoot`,
  `checkWlAvailable`, `claimWorkItem`, `clearFetchMemo`,
  `createInProcessRefreshScope`, `extractItems`, `extractJson`,
  `fetchActionableCount`, `fetchBlockersForItem`, `fetchChildrenForItem`,
  `fetchChildrenForItems`, `fetchCompletedItemCount`, `fetchItemDetails`,
  `fetchItemsByPriority`, `fetchItemsByStage`, `fetchNextItems`,
  `fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, `fetchReviewQueueState`, `getExecFileAsync`,
  `getInProcessOpenStats`, `getWlSpawnCap`, `getWorklogDir`,
  `markNeedsProducerReviewWorkItem`, `resetExecFileAsync`,
  `resetInProcessOpenStats`, `resetWlSpawnCap`, `resetWorklogDir`,
  `rollbackClaimWorkItem`, `runWlSync`, `setExecFileAsync`, `setWlSpawnCap`,
  `setWorklogDir`, `ReviewQueueState`.
- The live import graph already contains pre-existing cycles; the gate forbids a
  **new** cycle member or a new **runtime** cycle (parent AC4).

## Scope

- New **additive** test file `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts`
  (vitest).
- New `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts` — config, scanners
  and baseline producer for the fetcher family (mirrors `index-family.ts`).
- New committed baseline `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-baseline.json` —
  the 42 consumer-imported symbol names plus provenance (generation command,
  source commit, timestamp, scanned globs).
- **No production code moves. No existing test file is modified.**

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` exists and passes on the
   current (unsplit) tree **before any production code moves**; no existing test
   file is modified (parent AC3).
2. `fetcher.split-baseline.json` records the 42 consumer-imported symbol names
   with provenance, and is reproducible via
   `npx tsx packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts --write-baseline`
   (command recorded in the file and in the module doc comment).
3. **Public-surface gate:** every baseline symbol is still exported from
   `./fetcher.js` with its recorded kind (`value`/`type`); a removed or renamed
   symbol fails the test with the symbol name in the message.
4. **Size gate:** every `packages/herdr/src/fetcher*.ts` production module is
   ≤1,000 lines. The allowlist starts as `["fetcher.ts"]` (the pre-split
   monolith) and the test asserts the allowlist can only shrink — the final
   child empties it.
5. **Cycle gate:** the pre-existing cross-module cycle baseline is recorded in
   `fetcher-family.ts`; the gate fails on a new cycle member or a new
   **runtime** (non-type-only) cycle edge.
6. **Barrel-value-import gate:** no extracted `fetcher.*.ts` module may import
   the `./fetcher.js` barrel at runtime (type-only imports are allowed).
7. The guard suite runs green against the unsplit tree and is recorded as the
   evidence comment on this item.

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts`, importing the
   generic predicates from `./scan.ts` (never editing `scan.ts`); add only the
   fetcher-specific consumer discovery (static `./fetcher.js` imports across
   `src/**/*.ts`) and the baseline producer.
2. Generate and commit `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-baseline.json`.
3. Write `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` with the four gates
   (surface, size, cycle, barrel-value-import) and the allowlist-shrink
   assertion.
4. Run the guard suite via `/skill:test` (changed scope) and record the output
   in a comment on this item.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/fetcher-family.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-baseline.json` — new
- `packages/herdr/test/split-guard/scan.ts` — read-only (reused, never edited)
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — read-only (must not change)

## Dependencies

Blocks: every extraction child (2–7) and the close-out child (8).

## Notes

This child is the only one permitted to introduce the guard machinery. The
allowlist starts non-empty (the monolith itself) and only the final child may
empty it.

# Extract fetcher types and arg/exec primitives

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
**Source ranges (dev @ 4e69171d, 2,365 lines):** types 28–37, 277–375, 631–642, 760–785, 1073–1088, 1193–1209, 1717–1756, 1905–1945, 2142–2157 · `formatWlError` 37–66 · worklog-dir + wl-arg + exec seam 66–151
**New modules:** `fetcher.types.ts` (~250 lines), `fetcher.args.ts` (~140 lines)

## Goal

As a fetcher maintainer, I want the pure data types and the worklog-dir /
`wl`-argument / exec-seam primitives in dedicated leaf modules, so that changing
a type or the CLI invocation shape no longer means scrolling through 2,365 lines
of runtime logic.

## Scope (move-only)

Move **verbatim** (with provenance comments and section banners):

- **`fetcher.types.ts`:** `WlError`, `WorkItem`, `BlockerRef`,
  `DependencyTargetRef`, `ReviewQueueState`, `InProcessOpenStats`,
  `InProcessRefreshScope`, `WorklistBundle`, `RootSubstitution`,
  `ClaimResult`, and the internal `InProcessDb`/`InProcessDbCtor` type
  declarations.
- **`fetcher.args.ts`:** `formatWlError`, `setWorklogDir`, `getWorklogDir`,
  `buildWlArgs`, `buildWlArgsForRoot`, `resetWorklogDir`, `setExecFileAsync`,
  `getExecFileAsync`, `resetExecFileAsync`.

Do **not** move behaviour, rename a symbol, re-order a union/`Record` member, or
drop a doc comment. Leave every runtime fetch function for its own child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `fetcher.types.ts` and `fetcher.args.ts` exist and each is ≤1,000 lines
   (`wc -l`); the split-guard size gate passes with the allowlist unchanged
   (still only `fetcher.ts`).
2. Every moved symbol keeps its exact name, exported kind
   (`const`/`type`/`interface`/`function`), signature and value; the barrel
   re-exports each of the 42 consumer-imported symbols it hosts, no consumer
   file needs an import-path edit, and the public-surface gate passes.
3. `fetcher.types.ts` contains **only** type/interface declarations and
   `fetcher.args.ts` contains only the arg/exec primitives — no fetch function
   moves here.
4. Both new modules import only concrete siblings (never the `./fetcher.js`
   barrel); `fetcher.args.ts` may import types from `./fetcher.types.js` with
   `import type` only, so the cycle gate stays green.
5. The unmodified suites that exercise these primitives
   (`setWorklogDir.test.ts`, `claim.test.ts`, `fetcher-spawn-cap.test.ts`,
   `fetcher-timeout.test.ts`) pass, as does the full `packages/herdr` suite
   (`/skill:test`).
6. Each new module carries a one-line module doc comment naming its single
   responsibility; the original section banners and work-item ids move with
   their code.
7. `git diff` shows relocation, import rewiring and re-exports only — no logic
   edits; the `packages/herdr` build is green.

## Minimal implementation

1. Create `fetcher.types.ts`; move every pure-data type/interface verbatim.
2. Create `fetcher.args.ts`; move `formatWlError`, the worklog-dir trio, the
   `buildWlArgs*` pair and the exec seam verbatim.
3. Re-export the moved consumer-imported symbols from `fetcher.ts`; rewire the
   monolith's internal imports to the new modules.
4. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope) and the split-guard suite.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.types.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.args.ts` — new
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — remove moved blocks, add re-exports
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` — read-only gate

## Dependencies

Blocked by: split-guard child (1). Blocks: every later extraction child.

**Source ranges (dev @ 4e69171d):** CLI constants + memoization 506–577 · `wl` execution core 877–1033 (`isWlTimeoutError`, `runWlInner`, `queuedTimeout`, `runWlInnerUncapped`, `runWl`) · in-process SQLite reads 578–876 (`InProcessDb`, `openInProcessConnection`, `loadInProcessDbCtor`, `withInProcessDb`, `createInProcessRefreshScope`, `enrichInProcessItems`, stats)
**New modules:** `fetcher.cli.ts` (~280 lines), `fetcher.inprocess.ts` (~299 lines)

## Goal

As a fetcher maintainer, I want the `wl` CLI execution path (spawn, timeout,
retry, in-flight memo) and the in-process SQLite read path in separate modules,
so that a timeout/memo change and a database-read change are each reviewable
against their own tests.

## Scope (move-only)

- **`fetcher.cli.ts`:** `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `CLI_BINARIES`,
  `MEMOIZABLE_COMMANDS`, `MEMO_MAX_ENTRIES`, `WL_SPAWN_CAPPED_COMMANDS`,
  `inflightFetchMemo`, `fetchMemoKey`, `clearFetchMemo`, `_fetchMemoSize`,
  `isWlTimeoutError`, `queuedTimeout`, `runWlInner`, `runWlInnerUncapped`,
  `runWl`.
- **`fetcher.inprocess.ts`:** `InProcessDb`, `InProcessDbCtor`,
  `InProcessOpenStats`, `getInProcessOpenStats`, `resetInProcessOpenStats`,
  `openInProcessConnection`, `loadInProcessDbCtor`, `withInProcessDb`,
  `InProcessRefreshScope`, `createInProcessRefreshScope`,
  `enrichInProcessItems`.

Do not change: the 60 s default timeout, the memoizable-command set, the
memo TTL/entry cap, the in-flight dedup key, the fail-open fallback to the CLI
path when the in-process DB cannot open, or the timeout arithmetic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both modules exist and are ≤1,000 lines; the split-guard size gate passes
   with the allowlist unchanged (still only `fetcher.ts`).
2. Every moved symbol keeps its name, exported kind, signature and behaviour;
   the barrel re-exports each consumer-imported symbol
   (`DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `clearFetchMemo`,
   `createInProcessRefreshScope`, `getInProcessOpenStats`,
   `resetInProcessOpenStats`) and the public-surface gate passes.
3. **`fetcher.cli.ts` holds the only declaration of the in-flight memo**
   (`inflightFetchMemo`) and the only `runWl` implementation; the memo is still
   cleared by `clearFetchMemo()` and reports the same `_fetchMemoSize()`.
4. **`fetcher.inprocess.ts` holds the only declaration of the in-process open
   stats** and the only `createInProcessRefreshScope`; the DB-open counter still
   increments on the same events.
5. The in-process path stays strictly fail-open: any failure to load/open the
   DB returns `undefined`/falls back to the CLI path, never throws (existing
   behaviour).
6. Both new modules import only concrete siblings (`./fetcher.types.js`,
   `./fetcher.args.js`, `./fetcher.spawn-cap.js`, `./fetcher.json.js`) and
   never the `./fetcher.js` barrel; the cycle gate stays green.
7. The unmodified suites `fetcher-timeout.test.ts` (430 lines),
   `fetcher-inprocess.test.ts` (638), `large-db-spawn-cap.test.ts` (330),
   `fetcher-worklist-bundle.test.ts` (723) pass, as does the full

8. Module doc comments name each single responsibility; moved banners and
   work-item provenance comments travel with the code.
9. `git diff` shows relocation + import rewiring only; build green.

   core verbatim.
2. Create `fetcher.inprocess.ts`; move the in-process DB block verbatim.
3. Re-export the consumer-imported symbols from `fetcher.ts`; rewire monolith
   imports.
4. Run `/skill:test` (changed scope) + the split-guard suite.

**New modules:** `fetcher.root-substitution.ts` (~250 lines), `fetcher.api.ts` (~700 lines)

## Goal

As a fetcher maintainer, I want the critical-child root substitution and the
public fetch API in separate modules, so that the worklist-assembly pipeline and
the per-query fetch functions are each reviewable against their own tests.

## Scope (move-only)

- **`fetcher.root-substitution.ts`:** `MAX_ANCESTOR_HOPS`, `RootSubstitution`,
  `partitionCriticalItems`, `walkToRootAncestor`, `substituteCriticalRoots`,
  `ensureSubstitutedRoots`, **`mergeUniqueById`**, `mergeMandatoryAndSelect`,
  `assembleDefaultWorklist`.
  - `mergeUniqueById` moves here (not to the API module) because both the
    substitution tail and `fetchMandatorySubsets` use it; placing it in the
    lower module keeps the only edge `api → root-substitution` and avoids a
    cycle.
- **`fetcher.api.ts`:** `checkWlAvailable`, `fetchMandatorySubsets`,
  `fetchNextItems`, `fetchItemsByStage`, `fetchItemsByPriority`,
  `fetchItemDetails`, `fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, `fetchBlockersForItem`,
  `fetchActionableCount`, `runWlSync`, `fetchCompletedItemCount`,
  `fetchChildrenForItem`, `fetchChildrenForItems`, plus the internal
  `readChildrenInProcess`, `STAGE_STATUS` and `DEFAULT_WL_TIMEOUT_MS` use.

Do not change: the `MAX_ANCESTOR_HOPS` bound (32), the substitution semantics
(a critical child is represented by its root ancestor, never duplicated), the
audit-metadata merge, the `wl next -n` 32-item hard-cap workaround, the
fail-open fallback to the per-subset path, or any argument vector.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Both modules exist and are ≤1,000 lines; the split-guard size gate passes
   with the allowlist unchanged (still only `fetcher.ts`).
2. Every moved symbol keeps its name, exported kind, signature and behaviour;
   the barrel re-exports each consumer-imported symbol

   `fetchItemDetails`, `fetchItemsByPriority`, `fetchItemsByStage`,
   `fetchNextItems`, `fetchOutboundDepsForItems`, `runWlSync`) and the
   public-surface gate passes.
3. **`mergeUniqueById` is declared exactly once, in
   `fetcher.root-substitution.ts`**, and is not re-exported by the barrel
   (no consumer imports it today); the cycle gate stays green with a single
   `api → root-substitution` edge.
4. The default-worklist assembly stays identical: mandatory subsets are always
   included, a critical child is represented by its substituted root ancestor
   (WL-0MVN4WESM007T4XI), the richer `wl list` audit fields win the merge
   (WL-0MUWDW0N6003KF6G), and the count limits only the "other" items.
5. `fetchNextItems` still tries the consolidated bundle first and falls through
   to the per-subset path on any non-timeout failure; a hung `wl` still

# Finalise fetcher barrel, docs and close-out

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH47T007GKN1 — decompose `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts`
**Scope:** the residual `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` content (module doc
comment + import/export wiring) plus documentation updates and the final
verification pass for the epic.

## Goal

As a consumer of the fetcher, I want `fetcher.ts` to be a thin, honest barrel
that re-exports exactly the symbols other modules actually use, and I want the
herdr docs to show the module layout, so that the public surface is
discoverable and the epic's acceptance criteria are verifiable in one pass.

## Scope

- Reduce `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` to: a module-level doc comment (kept
  provenance, trimmed to a short overview + pointer to the module layout) and
  `export … from './fetcher.*.js'` statements only.
- Re-export **only the 42 symbols actually imported by consumers** (the frozen
  baseline from child 1); symbols that no consumer and no sibling module uses
  become internal.
- Empty the `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` in `fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` so the size gate
  now covers every `fetcher*.ts` module including the barrel.
- Documentation: add a "Module layout" section to
  `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` (or the most relevant herdr doc)
  listing module → single responsibility → key exports; update
  `packages/herdr/README.md` if it names fetcher internals; fix any code
  comments that still describe the monolith.
- Record the final verification evidence on the epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wc -l packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ≤ 250, and the file contains no
   function/type/const declarations — only the doc comment and re-exports.
2. The barrel re-exports exactly the 42 consumer-imported symbols from the
   baseline, and no symbol that neither a consumer nor a sibling module imports;
   a scan comparing barrel exports against the baseline (plus sibling-module
   imports) is recorded as evidence.
3. `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` is empty and the split-guard test proves every
   `packages/herdr/src/fetcher*.ts` production module (including the barrel) is
   ≤1,000 lines; the allowlist-shrink assertion is satisfied.
4. The split-guard public-surface, size, cycle and barrel-value-import gates all
   pass; no split module imports the barrel at runtime.
5. All 52 fetcher-related test suites plus the whole `packages/herdr` suite pass
   **unmodified**, and the full repo suite passes (`/skill:test` full).
6. The relevant `docs/dev/*.md` contains a "Module layout" section listing every
   module created by the split with its single responsibility, and no doc or
   comment still refers to `fetcher.ts` as a 2,365-line monolith; a search of
   the repository docs confirms no other page documents the old internal layout
   (result recorded in the evidence comment).
7. The build is green (`npm run build` in `packages/herdr`) and `tsc` reports
   no new errors.
8. A comment on this item records: `wc -l` output for every module, the guard
   test output, the suite result, and the symbol → module mapping — enough to
   audit epic AC1–AC5 without re-running anything.
9. Every epic AC (1–5) is verified with the evidence above; any AC that cannot
   be met is raised as an OPEN QUESTION on the epic instead of being silently
   waived.

## Minimal implementation

1. Delete the remaining moved code from `fetcher.ts`; build the barrel export
   list from the baseline JSON (and sibling-module imports) so it is exactly the
   used surface.
2. Empty `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST`; run the guard suite and inspect each gate's output.
3. Rewrite the module doc comment: short overview, the fail-open contract and a
   pointer to the module-layout table in the docs.
4. Add the docs module-layout section; update `packages/herdr/README.md` if it
   references internals.
5. Run `/skill:test` (full) + build; record the evidence comment; verify
   epic AC1–AC5.
6. Verify moved blocks match the pre-split source
   (`git show <pre-split>:packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` diff review) and note
   the result.

**Key Files:**

- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — becomes the thin barrel
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.split-guard.test.ts` — allowlist emptied
- `docs/dev/herdr-event-driven-refresh.md` — module layout section
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — internal references, if any
- all `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.*.ts` — read-only verification

## Dependencies

Blocked by: claim child (7). Final child of the epic.

## Notes

This child is the only one permitted to change the barrel's exported symbol set.
Removing an unused re-export is intended — but a symbol that a test file imports
is *used* and must stay, because test files may not be modified (parent AC3).

WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and the in-progress `src/github.ts` guard
(`tests/github/github-split-guard-scan.ts`, WL-0MVVLXSQX0031IB3) already

   predicate (`src/github-sync.ts` + `src/github-sync/**`) and gate predicates,

# Refactor guard: init split invariants

**Parent:** WL-0MVGKH6Z1000XWGJ — decompose `src/commands/init.ts` god class
**Type:** task (test-first gate — created and landed BEFORE any code moves)
**Position in chain:** 1 of 7 — blocks every extraction child.

## Goal

As a reviewer/auditor of the `src/commands/init.ts` split, I want one automated
gate that fails whenever the split breaks a behaviour-preserving invariant, so
that every extraction child can land safely, no existing test assertion changes,
and no reviewer has to re-derive the invariants by hand.

## Context

Parent AC1/AC2/AC3/AC4 require: no file over 1,000 lines, an unchanged public
surface at `./init.js`, unmodified test assertions, and an acyclic import graph.
Nothing in the repo enforces this for `src/commands/init*.ts` today. This child
builds the enforcement first, mirroring `tests/sync/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVP9MSJO0099V0G) and `tests/interview/split-guard.test.ts`
(WL-0MVXY34A900816MN).

Facts captured at plan time (2026-11-03, `dev`):

- `src/commands/init.ts` — 1,515 lines; public surface is exactly
  **2 exports**: default `register(ctx: PluginContext)` and named
  `isSorraAgentsInstalled(): boolean`.
- Consumers of `./init.js`: `src/command-registry.ts` (dynamic import, default)
  and `tests/cli/cli-inproc.ts` (default import). No external consumer imports
  `isSorraAgentsInstalled`, but it must stay importable (parent AC2).
- Three brittle **source-text** tests in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` read
  `src/commands/init.ts` with `fs.readFileSync` and assert hook-content strings
  (`tmp-worktree`, `git-common-dir`, `git-dir`, `const postCheckoutContent`,
  two `const centralScriptContent` occurrences). Those tests will break when
  child 4 moves the hook generators to `init.hooks.ts`.
- `tests/cli/init.test.ts` (584 lines) and `tests/cli/initialization-check.test.ts`
  (201 lines) are black-box CLI tests; they do not import init internals.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. New **additive** guard `tests/cli/init/split-guard.test.ts` passes on the
   current tree before any production code moves.
2. Committed baseline `tests/cli/init/init.split-baseline.json` records the two
   public exports (value/default flagged separately) plus provenance (generation
   command, source commit, timestamp).
3. Public exports from the original module path remain importable unchanged
   (barrel re-export where consumers exist): default `register` and named
   `isSorraAgentsInstalled` are still importable from `src/commands/init.js`.
4. No file (original or extracted module) exceeds 1,000 lines — the size gate
   enforces the ceiling for every `src/commands/init*.ts` production module,
   driven by an exported `SPLIT_ALLOWLIST` that initially contains only
   `'init.ts'`; a further assertion proves the allowlist only ever shrinks.
5. No new circular imports; module responsibilities documented — no production
   `src/commands/init*.ts` module contains a runtime import of `./init.js`, and
   the static import graph of `init*.ts` modules is acyclic.
6. Hook-content gate: the concatenated `src/commands/init*.ts` family source
   still contains `tmp-worktree`, `git-common-dir`, `git-dir`,
   `const postCheckoutContent`, and two `const centralScriptContent` blocks —
   so the hook generators remain behaviour-preserving wherever they live.
7. All existing tests pass without modification to their import paths or
   assertions (move-only, behaviour-preserving) — the three source-text tests
   in `tests/sync-worktree.test.ts` are generalised to read the whole
   `src/commands/init*.ts` family (concatenated) instead of only `init.ts`.
   **Assertion logic is unchanged** — only the source location is generalised
   so the tests pass before and after child 4. This is the only existing-test
   edit in the epic (see OPEN QUESTION below).
8. Each gate is proven to fail on a deliberately broken input (a synthetic
   >1,000-line module, a dropped export, a runtime barrel import, a removed
   hook-content string) — failure modes are unit-tested, not assumed.
9. `/skill:test` (changed scope) passes, including the new guard suite.
10. A comment records the baseline generation command and the gate-to-parent-AC
